question: Which Polypedilum/Pv11 recovery-associated molecular families are plausible bacterial-cellulose modifiers, and what observation would falsify each proposed mechanism?

source_anchors.finding: PvLEA4 is highly hydrophilic, desiccation inducible and limits aggregation of dehydration-sensitive proteins.
Multiple PvLEA genes show distinct expression profiles across desiccation and rehydration.
Pv PIMT paralogs show heterogeneous desiccation/rehydration expression; selected paralogs retain canonical methyltransferase activity under tested conditions.
Trehalose pretreatment activates a broad Pv11 anhydrobiosis program including LEA, thioredoxin, PIMT and LIL genes.
STRT1 contributes to trehalose export during rehydration; knockout slows trehalose release and morphological recovery.
Pv11 rehydration includes recovery-associated DNA-repair programs and molecularly distinct trehalose-treated, desiccated and rehydrated states.

candidate_families.known_property: compatible solute; water replacement and vitrification; osmotic and carbon-source effects
candidate_families.bc_hypothesis: Changes osmolarity, water activity and carbon availability around Komagataeibacter and can therefore alter BC yield or architecture.
candidate_families.critical_control: Quantitative trehalose-matched control plus post-wash carryover measurement.
candidate_families.falsifier: The Pv11-associated phenotype disappears after trehalose matching/removal or is fully reproduced by trehalose alone.

candidate_families.known_property: highly hydrophilic molecular shield; anti-aggregation; drying-induced structuralization
candidate_families.bc_hypothesis: If released or surface-exposed, LEA material may alter hydration shells, polymer interfaces, fibril bundling or nucleation.
candidate_families.critical_control: Defined recombinant protein or peptide exposure at matched ionic strength plus protein-only negative controls.
candidate_families.falsifier: Defined LEA exposure does not reproduce a cell-free recovery-fraction phenotype across independent BC batches.

candidate_families.known_property: redox control and ROS attenuation during desiccation/recovery
candidate_families.bc_hypothesis: A released redox-active factor could alter producer stress, local oxidative state or cellulose-synthesis physiology.
candidate_families.critical_control: Redox-matched controls and a direct ROS/redox readout.
candidate_families.falsifier: The matrix effect survives redox matching or defined redox manipulation fails to reproduce the phenotype.

candidate_families.known_property: protein L-isoaspartate repair methyltransferase activity for selected paralogs
candidate_families.bc_hypothesis: Direct extracellular BC action is weakly motivated; PIMT is stronger as a recovery-state marker or intracellular proteome-repair contributor.
candidate_families.critical_control: Do not infer a BC mechanism from PIMT expression alone.
candidate_families.falsifier: No extracellular PIMT/activity is detectable and defined exposure produces no BC phenotype.

candidate_families.known_property: anhydrobiosis-associated transmembrane proteins and candidate membrane protectants
candidate_families.bc_hypothesis: Recovery-dependent cell-surface state may alter adhesion, entrapment, nucleation geometry or local oxygen transport.
candidate_families.critical_control: Washed whole cells versus cell-free fraction with matched biomass and oxygen.
candidate_families.falsifier: Whole-cell specificity disappears after oxygen/contact matching or whole and cell-free fractions become equivalent after soluble-factor matching.

next_action: Prioritize trehalose, LEA and contact/oxygen mechanisms; keep PIMT as a state-marker-first candidate unless extracellular evidence emerges.
